agenda_text:
This meeting will be held via teleconference only in order to reduce the risk of spreading COVID-
19 and pursuant to AB 361 and the County of Los Angeles Public Health Officer’s Order (revised
April 21, 2022). All votes taken during this teleconference meeting will be by roll call vote, and the
vote will be publicly reported.

HOW TO VIEW THE MEETING: No physical location from which members of the public may
observe the meeting and offer public comment will be provided. Please view the meeting, which will be
live streamed at https://malibucity.org/video and https://malibucity.org/VirtualMeeting.

HOW TO PARTICIPATE BEFORE THE MEETING: Members of the public are encouraged to
submit email correspondence to mlinden@malibucity.org before the meeting begins.

HOW TO PARTICIPATE DURING THE MEETING: Members of the public may speak during the
meeting through the Zoom application. You must first sign up to speak before the item you would like
to speak on has been called by the Chair and then you must be present in the Zoom conference to be
recognized.

Please visit https://malibucity.org/VirtualMeeting and follow the directions for signing up to speak and
downloading the Zoom application.

  Guide to the City Commission Proceedings

As a result of the Coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, the City is under a state of local emergency, as well as states of
emergency that have been declared in the County of Los Angeles, State of California, and a federal emergency
declared by the President of the United States. In order to reduce the risk of spreading COVID-19, the Commission
meeting will be open and public but conducted virtually because meeting in person would present imminent risks to
the health or safety of attendees. This way, the public, the staff, and the Commission will not be physically in the same
place.
The Oral Communication portion of the agenda is for members of the public to present items which are not listed on the
agenda but are under the subject matter jurisdiction of the Commission. Although no action may be taken, the Commission
and staff will follow up, at an appropriate time, on those items needing response. Each speaker is limited to three (3) minutes.
Members of the public wishing to speak during the meeting must participate through the Zoom application. You must first
sign up to speak before the item you would like to speak on has been called by the Chair and then you must be present in the
Zoom conference to be recognized. Please visit https://MalibuCity.org/VirtualMeeting and follow the directions for signing
up to speak and downloading the Zoom application.
Items in Consent Calendar Section A have already been considered by the Commission at a previous meeting where the
public was invited to comment, after which a decision was made. These items are not subject to public discussion at this
meeting because the vote taken at the previous meeting was final. Resolutions concerning decisions made at previous
meetings are for the purpose of memorializing the decision to assure the accuracy of the findings, the prior vote, and any
conditions imposed.
Items in Consent Calendar Section B have not been discussed previously by the Commission. If discussion is desired, an
item may be removed from the Consent Calendar for individual consideration. Commissioners may indicate a negative or
abstaining vote on any individual item by so declaring prior to the vote on the motion to adopt the entire Consent
Calendar. Items excluded from the Consent Calendar will be taken up by the Commission following the action on the Consent
Calendar. The Commission first will take up the items for which public speaker requests have been submitted. Public speakers
shall follow the rules as set forth under Oral Communication.
Old Business items have appeared on previous agendas but have either been continued or tabled to this meeting with no final
action having been taken. Public comment shall follow the rules as set forth under Oral Communication.
Items in New Business are items which are appearing for the first time for formal action. Public comment shall follow the
rules as set forth under Oral Communication.
Copies of the staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business described above are on file in the
office of the City Manager, and available upon request by emailing MLinden@MalibuCity.org.
The City Hall phone number is (310) 456-2489. To contact City Hall using a telecommunication device for the deaf (TDD),
please call (800) 735-2929 and a California Relay Service operator will assist you. In compliance with the Americans with
Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in this meeting, please contact Yolanda Bundy, Environmental
Sustainability Director, at (310) 456-2489, ext. 229. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make
reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting. [28 CFR 35.102-35.104 ADD Title II].
I hereby certify under penalty of perjury, under the laws of the State of California, that the foregoing agenda was posted in
accordance with the applicable legal requirements. Dated this 29th day of July 2022, at 8:00 a.m.

  ___________________________________
  Mary Linden, Executive Assistant

ITEM 2.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  Lloyd Ahern, President of Las Tunas Homeowners Association (HOA), stated the
  City had an unsafe Fourth of July holiday. He discussed a person who attacked
  several homes on July 3 and July 4 with an axe. He commended the Sheriff’s
  Department for its response. He stated he would meet with City staff tomorrow. He
  discussed fear in his community. He stated it was critical to catch the man before

  Ryan Embree discussed the Sheriff’s tower at 23555 Civic Center Way. He stated
  it should not be classified as an emergency device.

ITEM 2.B.  STAFF UPDATES

  Public Safety Director Dueñas reported the City Council directed staff to prepare
  two Requests for Proposals (RFP) for school safety, including a comprehensive
  assessment of security at schools, and for security personnel to be added at school
  sites. She stated staff was meeting with the Council’s ad hoc committee and school
  district representatives tomorrow. She stated there was another meeting tomorrow
  regarding installation of a KBUU antenna on the Michael Landon Center. She
  introduced Brad Yocum, one of the City’s two new Fire Safety Liaisons.

  Fire Safety Liaison Yocum discussed his experience with the Los Angeles County
  Fire Department, including brush clearance, fuel modification, and home
  hardening.

  Public Safety Director Dueñas discussed Public Safety changes with the adoption
  of the Fiscal Year 2022-2023 Budget. She announced Public Safety was now an
  official department in the City, and Sarah Kaplan was promoted to Emergency
  Services Coordinator. She commended Emergency Services Coordinator Kaplan
  for a well-deserved promotion. In response to Mr. Ahern, she confirmed staff and
  the Sheriff’s Department would meet with Las Tunas residents tomorrow.

  Public Safety Liaison Flores discussed an overnight parking operation last week to
  observe parking violation issues. He stated Las Tunas Beach had a higher
  concentration of recreational vehicles (RV) parked overnight. He stated
  approximately one-quarter of RVs appeared to be inhabited by homeless
  individuals. He stated the homeless count numbers should be released later this
  month. He announced a Homeless Connect Day was tentatively scheduled for
  September 22.

  Fire Safety Liaison Etcheverry discussed a small fire on Latigo Canyon today. He
  stated the cause was unknown, but it was determined that it did not involve a
  homeless encampment.

  Public Safety Liaison Flores stated 84 vehicles had been towed to the temporary

  Public Works Director DuBoux stated maintenance crews worked the holiday

  was terminating its project to install a pedestrian hybrid beacon on Pacific Coast

  A.  Sheriff Access to Gated Communities
  Recommended Action: 1) Review options for providing Los Angeles County
  Sheriff’s Deputies access to gated communities through the installation of
  emergency key systems; and 2) Provide a recommendation to the City Council to
  implement the preferred option, if appropriate.

  Public Safety Liaison Flores presented the report. He introduced Lost Hills Station
  (LHS) Deputy Brian Knott who oversees emergency access systems in Calabasas.

  Deputy Knott stated the Calabasas program was for unmanned, gated communities.
  He stated Westlake Village HOAs also agreed to install Knox boxes. He discussed
  the cost, which was paid for by the communities. He stated keys were provided

  Vice Chair Stewart thanked Deputy Knott for attending. He stated some City
  Councilmembers did not want the Sheriff’s Department to have access. He
  expressed support for installing the boxes. He suggested starting without an

  Ryan Embree discussed problems coordinating with HOAs. He stated installation

  Deputy Knott stated the cost for a box was under $1,000. He stated he issued keys

  Commissioner Anneet suggested beginning with a voluntary program.

  Deputy Knott discussed the process for a homeowner to purchase a box. He stated
  the supplier would contact LHS to complete the installation. He offered to assist
  with outreach through the LHS social media network.

  Commissioner Spiegel stated many HOAs did not have formal processes. He
  suggested the City conduct a robust campaign for voluntary participation.

MOTION  Vice Chair Stewart moved and Commissioner Anneet seconded a motion to provide
  a recommendation that: 1) the City conduct a community education campaign in
  support of a voluntary program for use of Knox box keys utilized by Lost Hills
  Sheriff’s Station to provide Sheriff’s Department emergency access to gated
  communities and gated properties; and 2) direct the Public Safety Commission to
  review the progress of the program after one year. The question was called, and the
  motion carried 4-0, Commissioner Gibbs absent.

Subject:  Wildfire Risk Factors

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Receive and file a report from the City’s Fire Safety Liaisons
on the factors that influence wildfire risk.

DISCUSSION:  As part of the City’s continuous wildfire preparedness, staff tracks Live
Fuel Moisture (LFM) in the Malibu area as an important part of determining current fire
conditions. LFM is the percentage of water content to dry matter in live vegetation. The
Los Angeles County Fire Department Forestry Division conducts sampling approximately
every two weeks and posts the results on its website. LFM can be as high as 200%, and
60% and below is considered critical. The historical average for this time of year is about
90% and, on July 13, the LFM was at 71%.

However, LFM is not the only factor for determining fire risk conditions. Critical fire weather
is comprised of several factors that can lead the National Weather Service (NWS) to issue
a Red Flag Warning, including temperature, relative humidity, and wind. A Red Flag
Warning indicates that a weather event will occur within 24 hours that may result in
extreme fire behavior. A Red Flag Warning is the highest alert. During these times,
extreme caution is urged for all residents because a simple spark can cause a major
wildfire. The NWS may also issue a Fire Weather Watch when this type of weather
condition could exist in the next 12 to 72 hours. A Fire Weather Watch is one level below
a warning, but fire danger is still high.

The City’s Fire Safety Liaisons will be available to answer any questions about these fire
risk factors.

  NOTEWORTHY INCIDENTS

  A robbery was reported in the 29100 block of Pacific Coast Highway. The suspect
  entered the location, showed a handgun to the victim/clerk and handed the victim a
  plastic bag. The victim attempted to open the cash register to give the suspect the
  cash inside but was unsuccessful. The suspect grabbed the bag back and took the
  victim’s cell phone and exited the location. The victim followed the suspect outside
  and began to chase him. The suspect then shot the victim in the leg and fled in a
  red Land Rover. (22-03036)

  A Malibu transient was arrested for assault in the area of Pacific Coast Highway
  and Serra Road. The victim was riding his bicycle in the area, saw some discarded
  property on the roadway and threw them away. As the victim was leaving the area,
  the suspect threw a dumbbell at him and hit the victim on the leg and damaged
  his electric bicycle. The property on the roadway belonged to the suspect.
  (22-03327)

  A transient from Malibu was arrested for committing two residential burglaries and
  an arson in the 3500 block of Coast View Drive and the 31600 block of Broad Beach
  Road. In one incident, the suspect found the key to the location and made entry
  without the permission of the owner. In the other incident, the suspect made entry
  into the victim’s unlocked vehicle and stole the garage remote control. The suspect
  then used the garage remote control to enter the home. The suspect set two
  fires outside the residence (wall of garage and near side gate). (22-03110, 03287)

  A Malibu transient was arrested for residential burglary in the 27400 block of Pacific
  Coast Highway. The suspect made entry via the unlocked front door. (22-03138)

  A transient from Malibu was arrested for residential burglary in the 21800 block of
  Pacific Coast Highway. Entry was made via the unlocked front door. (22-03192)

  Five vehicle burglary incidents were reported in the 27700 block of Pacific Coast
  Highway. The victims were in the area hiking. In two incidents, the vehicles
  windows were smashed, two vehicles had the door keyhole damaged and in

  were found in a trash can in front of the Malibu Pavilion store. One tracker was
  found inside the store. One the stolen credit cards was used at a business in the
  30700 block of Pacific Coast Highway. (22-02904, 02944, 03041, 03425, 03446)

the community. We also provide the parents with resource programs within our community.

charges against juvenile offenders.

investigations and current juvenile issues within our city.

related issues. We have worked with the narcotic detectives on several narcotic cases directly and indirectly

juvenile contacts with uniform personnel).

9. Conducted our normal checks of juvenile problem areas in the city during weekend evenings and responded
to juvenile related calls for service.

12. Month End Reports completed.

MINUTES
  MALIBU PUBLIC SAFETY COMMISSION
  REGULAR MEETING
  AUGUST 3, 2022
  TELECONFERENCED VARIOUS LOCATIONS
  -

  5:00 P.M.

The following meeting was held pursuant to AB 361 and fully teleconferenced from various
locations during the coronavirus disease (COVID-19) pandemic.

CALL TO ORDER

  Chair Frost called the meeting to order at 5:00 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Chair Chris Frost; Vice Chair Doug Stewart; Commissioners Daphne Anneet,
  and Joshua Spiegel; and Ex Officio Member Brent Woodworth

  ABSENT:  Commissioner Keegan Gibbs

  ALSO PRESENT:  Rob DuBoux, Public Works Director; Luis Flores, Public Safety
  Liaison; Gabe Etcheverry, Fire Safety Liaison; Greg Hisel, Fire Safety Liaison; Brad
  Yocum, Fire Safety Liaison; Brandie Ayala, Senior Administrative Assistant; Parker
  Davis, Media Technician; Lieutenant Dustin Carr, Los Angeles County Sheriffs
  Department; Assistant Fire Chief Andrew Smith, Los Angeles County Fire Department;
  Community Services Liaison Megan Currier, Los Angeles County Fire Department; and
  Mary Linden, Executive Assistant

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Fire Safety Liaison Hisel led the Pledge of Allegiance.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Chair Frost moved, and Commissioner Spiegel seconded a motion to approve the
  agenda. The question was called, and the motion carried 4-0, Commissioner Gibbs
  absent.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Executive Assistant Linden reported that the agenda for the meeting was properly posted
  onJuly 29, 2022.

ITEM 1  CEREMONIAL / PRESENTATIONS

  None.

ITEM 2.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  None.

ITEM 2.B.  STAFF UPDATES

  Public Safety Liaison Flores discussed homeless outreach. He stated the outreach
  team was filling in while Deputy Espinosa was out. He stated the County’s
  homeless count numbers should be available by next meeting. He announced the
  Homeless Connect Day on September 22. He stated 10 vehicles were towed this
  past weekend for a total of 167 since the tow yard began operation. He stated
  automatic license plate reader (ALPR) cameras were ordered and expected to be
  delivered in August. He stated the Knox box item, including community education
  plans, was tentatively scheduled to go to the City Council on September 12.

  Fire Safety Liaison Hisel stated he was working on developing a local policy for
  fire weather local emergencies and had submitted an outline to the Assistant City
  Manager. In response to Chair Frost, Fire Safety Liaison Hisel discussed his
  background.

  Fire Safety Liaison Yocum discussed home ignition zone assessments. He stated
  community interest was picking up.

  In response to Chair Frost, Public Safety Liaison Flores stated he would share the
  flyer for the Homeless Connect Day with the Commissioners.

  Emergency Services Coordinator Kaplan stated there were four graduates from the
  in-person CERT training program last weekend with more finishing missed classes.
  She announced Fire Department Community Services Liaison Megan Currier
  would be at City Hall to distribute NOAA fire radios on Thursday, August 18, from
  9:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. She stated several events were being planned for National
  Preparedness Month in September.

  Public Works Director DuBoux discussed generators for Los Angeles County
  Waterworks District 29 (District 29). He stated temporary generators were out in
  Big Rock. He stated District 29 would ensure water tanks were full if the generators
  had to be moved. He stated truck-mounted portable generators were ready to deploy
  when needed. He discussed Caltrans’ public meeting last month about removing
  parking to add bike lanes on PCH. He stated he had advised Caltrans about the
  problems with that plan. He discussed options he suggested to Caltrans for bike
  lane improvements. He discussed the Trancas Bridge Replacement Project,
  including soundproofing.

  Chair Frost stated he thought there would be permanent generators in Big Rock for
  when the power goes out. In response to Chair Frost, Public Works Director
 Malibu Public Safety Commission
Regular Meeting
Minutes of August 3, 2022
Page 3 of 7

  DuBoux stated he was not sure if there was an automatic switch at Big Rock, but
  he would check and report back. He stated the pump stations had quick connections
  to attach the generators.

  Ex Officio Member Woodworth suggested asking District 29 to place a temporary
  generator with automatic transfer if one had to be moved. He asked if Caltrans
  commented why they did not consult with the Coastal Commission before the
  public meeting. Public Works Director DuBoux stated that was the City’s advice.

  In response to Vice Chair Stewart, Public Works Director DuBoux stated he did
  not have answers yet about why traffic signal backup power did not work during
  power outage last month.

Chair Frost reopened Public Comment.

ITEM 2.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  Ryan Embree stated notifications to homeowners associations (HOA) advising
  them to renew Letters of Agency and to promote Knox Boxes should be sent. He
  stated a one-year expiration for Letters of Agency was too short. He stated it had
  been four months since he requested an update on deaths in Trancas. He stated it
  should not take that long for a coroner’s report.

ITEM 2.C.  COMMISSIONER COMMENTS

  Ex Officio Member Woodworth thanked Public Safety Liaison Flores for the
  update on the impound yard. He stated the community fire brigade was in contact
  with CAL FIRE. He requested being allowed to participate in the tabletop exercise.

  Commissioner Spiegel welcomed Lieutenant Can. He discussed the use of about
  200 goats for brush clearance in Malibu West. He stated it brought the community
  together and enhanced rural character. He suggested exploring grants, including
  CAL FIRE grants, for more goat brush clearing.

  Vice Chair Stewart welcomed the Fire Safety Liaisons. In response to Vice Chair
  Stewart, Fire Safety Liaison Etcheverry stated map validation was completed for
  the Beacon Boxes. He stated staff was waiting for the second set often boxes from
  FlameMapper. He discussed properties selected for installation. He stated seven
  boxes would be installed this week. In response to Vice Chair Stewart, Fire Safety
  Liaison Etcheverry stated approximately 20 boxes would be up and running within
  a month or so.

  Vice Chair Stewart requested an update on the bailment agreement for the
  Volunteers on Patrol (VOP) car. Public Works Director DuBoux stated the car was
 Malibu Public Safety Commission
Regular Meeting
Minutes of August 3, 2022
Page 4 of 7

  being equipped. Chair Frost stated it still had to be approved by the Board of
  Supervisors.

  Vice Chair Stewart asked if evacuation zone signage would be installed on Pacific
  Coast Highway (PCH). Emergency Services Coordinator Kaplan stated staff was
  working with the Los Angeles County Fire Department and Office of Emergency
  Management (OEM) on the Zone Haven maps. She stated signage was on hold until
  that was completed.

  Public Works Director DuBoux stated he was working with the Sheriffs
  Department on recreational vehicle (RV) shoulder parking, including on Trancas.
  He stated temporary signs about the oversized vehicle ordinance were installed at
  the request of the Sheriffs Department and on recommendation from the Planning
  Department so deputies could cite the vehicles. Public Safety Liaison Flores stated
  the Sheriffs request came afier a recent overnight operation focused on overnight
  parking along PCH. He thanked Public Works for a quick response.

  Vice Chair Stewart stated his HOA was installing Flock ALPR cameras. He
  discussed problems with cell signals on PCH. He discussed protests at the Malibu
  Democratic Club forum for County Supervisor candidates over the weekend. He
  commended the Sheriffs Department and local security for keeping them from
  disrupting the event.

  Chair Frost commended staff for the oversized vehicle ordinance signage. He stated
  consistent enforcement was important. He discussed the 1 80s (ticket to tow that
  must be written and attached to the car being towed) issued. He stated the VOP
  could not issue a 180. He expressed concern that there may not be sufficient
  community services officers (CSO) on duty during hot weather days for all the
  vehicles that should be towed.

ITEM 3  CONSENT CALENDAR
